script.title: Exempt vs Nil-rated vs Zero-rated Supply
script.caption_hook: Both say "no tax", but only one keeps your ITC. Which one?

lines.say: Both mean no tax, but one keeps ITC? How?
Good question! No tax has two families. Let's separate them.
Exempt means no tax payable, and inputs get no ITC. Nil-rated, wholly exempt and non-taxable supplies all count.
Nil-rated too? I thought zero meant refund.
Nil-rated is a domestic supply at 0% rate, so it's exempt. Refund belongs to zero-rated supply.
Export of goods or services, or supply to an SEZ developer or unit for authorised operations.
What if the goods are exempt when sold locally?
Still zero-rated if exported. ITC stays and refund can be claimed, even if the same goods are exempt at home.
And a business with both exempt and taxable sales?
Only exclusive-use ITC is blocked. Common input ITC is reversed in proportion to exempt supplies.
Got it! Zero zooms out with a refund, exempt eats ITC.
Exactly. Remember: zero zooms out with refund, exempt eats the ITC.

check_notes: Writer: Basis: Sec 17(2)/17(3) CGST proportional reversal mentioned only generally; no rates or limits stated. Word count approx 150.

Checker: Line 1 / Line 2 / board title 'No Tax, Two Types': the script presents zero-rated supply as a 'no tax' supply. Under Section 16(3) of the IGST Act, a zero-rated supply can be made either under a bond/LUT without paying IGST, with a refund of unutilised ITC, or with IGST paid and then refunded (the second route is limited to notified cases). Suggested wording: 'Both end up tax-free, but only one keeps ITC', and say once that zero-rated supply can also be made with IGST paid and refunded.

Checker: Line 12: 'Only exclusive-use ITC is blocked' is loose. Under Section 17(2) read with Rule 42, ITC on inputs used only for exempt supplies is not available, and common ITC is reversed in the ratio of exempt turnover to total turnover. Suggested wording: 'reversed in the ratio of exempt turnover to total turnover'.
